scenarios.name: honest_boot
scenarios.description: Provision three stages, arm, measure MBR -> ESP -> loader in order with the right digests, then use the media and grant a password-authorized erase.

steps.note: reset released; lock idle, no golden vector yet
fixture writes golden for the ESP
fixture writes golden for the loader; fuse burnt
platform presents a UEFI boot source
hdparm: SECURITY UNLOCK after freeze -> refused

scenarios.name: tampered_mbr
scenarios.description: The bootstrap on the disk does not match the golden vector. Everything after that must be denied, and the destructive-command refusal is the point.

steps.note: attacker then presents a good ESP: refused, lock is closed
boot source presented to a locked chipset
hdparm: SECURITY ERASE UNIT -> denied by chipset policy
recovery strap: re-provisioning only, not erasure
reflash while recovery strap is asserted -> still denied on a tampered box

scenarios.name: stage_skip
scenarios.description: A loader that skips straight to the ESP, i.e. an attempt to reorder or omit a stage. Order violation latches immediately.

scenarios.name: boot_mode_policy
scenarios.description: UEFI-only policy. The legacy MBR path is refused even with a perfect chain, and vice versa.

steps.note: legacy/CSM source presented under a UEFI-only policy

scenarios.name: provision_attack
scenarios.description: After the first accepted measurement the reference vectors are frozen. A late provisioning attempt is refused and (by policy) is treated as tamper.

steps.note: rewrite the root of trust to match the attacker
everything after the violation is inert

scenarios.name: attempt_counter
scenarios.description: Five wrong passwords exhaust the ATA attempt counter. With destructive operations denied by policy the device cannot be recovered in-band, which is the documented cost of refusing to erase.

steps.note: the correct password no longer unlocks
hdparm: SECURITY ERASE UNIT -> policy denies destructive history erasure
writes were already blocked by the locked drive

scenarios.name: recovery_strap
scenarios.description: Physical presence before first handoff re-opens provisioning so a fixture can re-key the device. It never grants erasure and never reflashes a tampered box.

steps.note: recovery strap asserted: no help, the latch is not pre-boot any more
fixture cycle: power-on reset with the strap held
vendor reflash during recovery: refused, chain not complete
re-keyed device hands control to the measured stage

scenarios.name: prov_race
scenarios.description: A provisioning violation landing in the same cycle as a valid measurement. The attack must win: the measurement is refused and the lock latches, instead of leaving tampered-but-not-locked for a cycle. The SAT solver found this race, so it is pinned here.

steps.note: violation and measurement in the same cycle
the chain can never complete after this
